In [[abstract algebra|algebra]], the '''Artin–Tate lemma''', named after [[John Tate (mathematician)|John Tate]] and his former advisor [[Emil Artin]], states:<ref>[[David Eisenbud|Eisenbud, David]], ''Commutative Algebra with a View Toward Algebraic Geometry'', Graduate Texts in Mathematics, 150, Springer-Verlag, 1995, {{ISBN|0-387-94268-8}}, Exercise 4.32</ref>
:Let ''A'' be a [[commutative ring|commutative]] [[Noetherian ring]] and <math>B \sub C</math> [[commutative algebra (structure)|commutative]] [[algebra over a ring|algebras over ''A'']]. If ''C'' is of finite type over ''A'' and if ''C'' is finite over ''B'', then ''B'' is of finite type over ''A''.
(Here, "of finite type" means "[[finitely generated algebra]]" and "finite" means "[[finitely generated module]]".) The lemma was introduced by E. Artin and J. Tate in 1951<ref>E Artin, J.T Tate, "A note on finite ring extensions," J. Math. Soc Japan, Volume 3, 1951, pp. 74–77</ref> to give a [[mathematical proof|proof]] of [[Hilbert's Nullstellensatz]].

The lemma is similar to the [[Eakin–Nagata theorem]], which says: if ''C'' is finite over ''B'' and ''C'' is a Noetherian ring, then ''B'' is a Noetherian ring.

== Proof ==

The following proof can be found in  Atiyah–MacDonald.<ref>[[Michael Atiyah|M. Atiyah]], [[Ian G. Macdonald|I.G. Macdonald]], ''[[Introduction to Commutative Algebra]]'', [[Addison–Wesley]], 1994. {{ISBN|0-201-40751-5}}. Proposition 7.8</ref> Let <math> x_1,\ldots, x_m</math> generate <math>C</math> as an <math>A</math>-algebra and let <math>y_1, \ldots, y_n</math> generate <math>C</math> as a <math>B</math>-module. Then we can write

:<math>x_i = \sum_j b_{ij}y_j \quad \text{and} \quad y_iy_j = \sum_{k}b_{ijk}y_k</math>

with <math>b_{ij},b_{ijk} \in B</math>. Then <math>C</math> is finite over the <math>A</math>-algebra <math>B_0</math> generated by the <math>b_{ij},b_{ijk}</math>. Using that <math>A</math> and hence <math>B_0</math> is Noetherian, also <math>B</math> is finite over <math>B_0</math>. Since <math>B_0</math> is a finitely generated <math>A</math>-algebra, also <math>B</math> is a finitely generated <math>A</math>-algebra.

== Noetherian necessary ==
Without the assumption that ''A'' is Noetherian, the statement of the Artin–Tate lemma is no longer true. Indeed, for any non-Noetherian ring ''A'' we can define an ''A''-algebra structure on <math>C = A\oplus A</math> by declaring <math>(a,x)(b,y) = (ab,bx+ay)</math>. Then for any [[ideal (ring theory)|ideal]] <math>I \subset A</math> which is not finitely generated, <math>B = A \oplus I \subset C</math> is not of finite type over ''A'', but all conditions as in the lemma are satisfied.
